title: Wave Allocation for Cross-Functional Micro-Cycles (Platform & Product Sync)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce cross-team context switching and increase predictable delivery by piloting 'wave' micro-cycles that stagger platform, infra, and product work. The wave model splits a two-week cycle into overlapping 5-day focused windows for specific streams (Platform, Core Runtime, Console, Integrations). Each stream gets a focused work window plus a 24-48h handoff/triage buffer to absorb emergent work.

Why now: Current cycles show frequent mid-cycle scope churn when infra incidents or urgent platform migrations collide with product roadmaps. This causes commit slippage and higher deferral rates. A deliberate wave model aims to: reduce interruption, guarantee a minimum throughput per stream, and make short-term staffing tradeoffs explicit.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Increase % of committed work completed per cycle from baseline 72% to >=85% for participating teams.
- Reduce mid-cycle unplanned pull-ins measured as tasks created with label 'hot' by 40%.
- Mean time to resume (context switch cost) after interruption reduced by 25% measured via time-tracking polls and pair logs.

Scope: Pilot with 3 teams: Platform (batching/KV cache work), Runtime (kernel scheduling), and Console (rollouts and observability). Exclude customer-facing launch-heavy initiatives during pilot. Pilot runs 3 cycles (6 weeks).

Approach:
1) Define Wave Calendar: Map each cycle's 5-day wave per stream and an overlapping 2-day buffer for handoffs.
2) Reserve Capacity: Each stream must protect 10% of FTE capacity for hotfixes; leadership can reassign up to additional 5% only with documented tradeoff.
3) Scope Contracts: During a wave, participating teams commit to no new epics without a scoped triage vote; PMs maintain a 'wave backlog' prioritized for the next wave.
4) Measurement: Instrument cycle dashboards with new KPIs (commit completion rate, hot pull-in rate, switch downtime).
5) Retro checkpoints: Weekly waves retro + cross-functional report at end of pilot.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Risk: Longer delay for cross-team dependent work if wave windows are misaligned. Mitigation: explicit dependency slots in calendar and one 'open day' mid-cycle for cross-team syncs.
- Tradeoff: Might reduce flexibility for urgent customer requests; mitigation is the reserved capacity and clear escalation path via SRE/Oncall.
- Operational overhead: Maintaining wave calendar and enforcing scope contracts will require 0.25 PM/Team-week overhead during pilot.

Artifacts & links:
- Wave pilot PRD: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WavePilotPRD (internal)
- Pilot calendar (read-only): https://calendar.redwood-inference.com/wave-pilot-2026
- Prototype dashboard for metrics: https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/wave-metrics/pilot
- Example playbook for handoffs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HandoffPlaybook

Stakeholders: Sarah Gold (VP Product), Rajiv Menon (Head of Platform), Elena Park (Head of Eng Ops), SRE leads, Design liaison for Console.

Next steps: Finalize pilot calendar, secure participating squads and capacity commitments, add dashboards to Console beta, and schedule kickoff sync (target 2026-03-15).
decisions: Pilot length fixed to 3 cycles (6 weeks)
Protect 10% FTE per stream for hotfixes; additional 5% reassign only via documented tradeoff
Include one mid-cycle cross-team open day for dependency work
